Now the Marquis, the ruler of Tyre,
because a dispute had fallen out between him and the King of England,
for the reason that he had not permitted him to rule Tyre as his own,
and he wanted to take Tyre from him,
therefore he had promised Saladin that he would side with the Arabs (Tayyaye),
and take up the fight against those of his own race.
And while his envoy on this matter was with Saladin,
two Ismaili men, in the disguise of monks, attacked the Marquis while he was riding.
And when one of them struck him with a knife,
his companion fled to a church that was nearby.
As for the Marquis, who had been struck,
they likewise brought him into that church.
And when the Ismaili monk, the companion of the one who had struck him, saw
that he was still speaking,
he also leapt upon him inside the church and repeated the blow,
and he died immediately.
And when the Franks seized both of these Ismailis
and tortured them, they said
that the King of England had sent them.
And because of the hatred that existed between them,
the Franks believed the words of these murderers.
But in the end it was revealed
that Sinan, the chief of the Ismailis, had sent them.
Then the King of England gave Tyre to Count Henry,
and he married the wife of the Marquis,
and went in unto her while she was pregnant,
an unlawful act.
And the Franks gathered strength and went and attacked Darum,
and took it by storm from the Arabs,
and killed everyone who was in it.
And at that time the Franks captured a great caravan of the Arabs that was coming from Egypt,
bringing gold to Saladin.
And Saladin heard that with a great force the Franks were preparing to march against Jerusalem,
and he sent and gathered his armies,
and prepared for battle.
And he fortified the walls of Jerusalem,
and destroyed all the cisterns of water outside Jerusalem.
And when the Franks prepared to advance against Jerusalem,
the King of England did not permit them.
